official_rules_as_stated.as_stated: Approved countries are in three groups. Group 2 (recognised by DAFF as rabies-free) includes Japan, Hawaii, Guam, Iceland and Singapore. Group 3 (rabies present but well controlled) includes the United States except Hawaii and Guam, Canada, the United Kingdom, listed EU member states, and South Korea. Animals from a non-approved origin must first reside 180 days in an approved country. A valid biosecurity import permit is required in most cases, applied for through BICON.
The microchip must be ISO-compatible (10 or 15 digits). Numbers starting with 999, and 9-digit AVID chips, are not accepted. Pet passports are not accepted as the import document.

Group 3 rabies pathway: vaccination from 84 days of age; an RNATT (FAVN or RFFIT) of at least 0.5 IU/ml; the sample taken between 12 months and 180 days before export; and a 180-day wait from the date the sample arrives at the laboratory (this is a residency period, not quarantine). If vaccination or the RNATT lapses, the 180-day wait restarts.

Arrival for post-entry quarantine (PEQ) imports is at Melbourne International Airport only, as manifested cargo in an IATA crate (assistance dogs may be exempt from the cabin rule — see the K9 section). There is no domestic transfer into Melbourne for that arrival. A biosecurity officer takes the animal to Mickleham PEQ, 135 Donnybrook Road, Mickleham VIC 3064. Home quarantine is not allowed. Group 3 quarantine is 30 days, or 10 days with the official identity check (or Australian-origin export certification). Group 2 dogs stay at least 10 days. A stay can be extended up to 180 days if there is a biosecurity issue.

A titre below 0.5 IU/ml, a missing test, or a missing or mismatched microchip can lead to an extended quarantine at the owner’s expense. APQA states that the average extended quarantine is 10 days and that the period can be longer depending on the case. Without a health certificate, the animal must be returned to the exporting country at the owner’s cost.
